Drag a knob up/down (or scroll, or use arrow keys) to turn it. Double-click to reset. Bass Boost shelves up the low end; Reverb blends in a convolved room decay; Filter sweeps a low-pass to the left of center and a high-pass to the right; Distortion drives a soft-clip waveshaper; Bitcrush crushes bit depth and sample rate for a lo-fi/glitch sound; Echo repeats the signal with decaying slap-back delays; Tremolo pulses the volume rhythmically. All run through the same Web Audio graph as the equalizer.

Latency
Latency 0 ms
-2000 ms (delay sound)+2000 ms (delay picture)

Delays the picture and subtitles to match audio arriving late over Bluetooth. Positive values hold the video and subtitles back; negative values shift subtitle timing earlier.

Set this once for your earbuds, then tap the button to switch it on or off instead of resetting the slider each time.

Runs the latency delay on the GPU, which stops heavy videos dropping frames. Trade-offs: uses more graphics memory, needs WebGL2, may use a little more battery than the plain video player, and colours can differ slightly (HDR is not tone-mapped). Turn it off if a video looks wrong or the delay misbehaves; the older method is used instead.

A line sweeps across the ruler and a click plays the instant it crosses each bar. Watch the bar you hear the click on, read its number, and set the slider to that.

Video enhancement

Frame interpolation and sharper scaling for video. Each can go on the quick bar as its own pill.

Motion smoothing
Motion smoothing
Smooth videos up to50 fps
Output up to120 fps
Advanced strength50%
Smoothing quality

Adds in-between frames to low-fps video. Simple suits low-end devices, Advanced tracks motion and needs a decent GPU. "Smooth up to" skips videos faster than that (set 60 to smooth 60 fps video). "Output up to" caps how many frames per second are shown; lower saves battery. Smoothing quality sets the resolution the smoothing works at (High and 4K need a strong GPU and lots of memory; the player steps down by itself if memory runs out). Adds about one frame of delay, covered by the latency setting.

Upscaling
Upscale up to

Sharper enlargement (bicubic) for when your screen has more pixels than the smoothing quality provides. It never goes above your screen's real resolution, so it only does something when your screen is larger than the smoothing resolution. Works together with Motion smoothing.

Level
Storage
—
Backup speedMax
Applies to both export and restore. Lower is slower but gentler on memory and battery. Try a low setting if the page crashes.
Video decoding
Frame-drop protection
Browsers decide hardware vs software decoding themselves, so this lightens everything else. Auto: if a video keeps skipping frames, filters, motion smoothing and UI animation switch off for that video. Light: always off while this is set.
Audio lead (no frame drops)
Instead of delaying the picture, plays the sound slightly ahead of the video by the latency amount. The video is never processed, so it can't drop frames. Subtitles stay with the picture. The visualizer is silent on video while this is on.
Decode compensation (+300 ms)
Adds a fixed 300 ms picture delay to every video to cover browser decoding lag.
Lossless latency (no dropped frames)
When the latency slider delays the picture, capture every decoded frame off the main thread instead of grabbing frames one at a time. Fixes videos losing frames while latency is on. Needs a Chromium-based browser; elsewhere the normal GPU delay is used. Motion smoothing still uses the GPU when it is on.
Delayed picture sharpness
Size of the frames held for the delay. Low is the original 640 px: lightest on memory but soft. High is sharper: Auto spends up to 512 MB (sharp for short delays, softer for long ones), and fixed widths are still shrunk if they would need over 2 GB.
Lighten UI while video plays
Animated gradient backgrounds and blur effects repaint behind the video and can cause dropped frames. Stop animation & blur freezes them during playback. Flatten gradients also turns gradient backgrounds into a solid colour. Everything returns when the video is paused.

Media player layout

            
Browse your library with a bottom tab bar and a mini-player. Tapping a video opens a full-screen player page; closing it brings you back to the library. Turn off to go back to the original layout.

          

          
        

      

      

        

          

            
Detailed playlist mode

            
Thumbnails, video size and length per track, plus multiple playlists.

          

          
        

      

      

        

          

            
Keep MP3 conversions on reload

            
On: a video converted to audio-only stays that way. Off: it switches back to video the next time the library loads.

          

          
        

      

      

        

          

            
Remember playback position

            
On: switching tracks or reopening the player picks up where you left off. Off: every track always starts from the beginning.
